item: R730: per-language person/organisation rejects (function words, Swedish demonyms, Finnish place genitives, Nordic event abbreviations); text_processor keeps script marks
refs: R730; field test 2026-11-14 rows 62 and 70; WWW_INDEXER_VERSION 2
key_paths: src/timemap/entextract.py; src/timemap/whostore.py; src/analytics/reindex_parallel.py; src/analytics/engine_identity.py; src/services/text_processor.py; tests/test_entextract_r730.py
summary: extract_entities takes the article's language (whostore, the pooled re-index, the reader, the perception harness pass it). Tested languages only (sv fi da nb nn no de en fr; none without a language): a person candidate is rejected when a token is in the language's grammar stoplist (minus given names that collide: Hans Olli Kai Ville Will May Ernst Ole), a Swedish definite demonym (-bon/-borna), or a Finnish -n/-en genitive of a gazetteer place (only with a gazetteer hit, so Johan or Kristian stay names); VM/EM/OS/SM/NM/DM are never organisations in the Nordic languages. Sample (9 languages, 18 real people, 7 field-shaped junk names): junk 7 -> 0, real names kept unchanged. The grammar stoplists joined the www data digest (WWW_SHARED_DATA_GLOBS) without leaving the keyword one. Not addressed: German and English capitalised role nouns ('Minister Olaf', 'Prime Minister') still read as people. The /api/keywords text processor now keeps non-Latin combining marks (the Latin decomposition it always did is unchanged).
